clue.text: A Manchester pub outing with an out-of-this-world character

indicators.note: an outing takes the pub phrase's letters out for a jaunt, rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written, placed after the anagram

explanation.surface: A group trip to a Manchester pub in the company of a rather unearthly companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' shuffles A MANCHESTER PUB, and AN follows it. The answer is the Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band's 1968 hit 'I'm the Urban Spaceman', and the band is this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman comes from outer space, so he is literally a character not of this world.

clue.text: Jumbo album by Fleetwood Mac starts to encounter ridicule

parts.note: Tusk is Fleetwood Mac's 1979 double album

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A huge Fleetwood Mac record that was greeted with mockery at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like an adjective describing the album, but it is the definition: a big elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and a tusker is an elephant with large tusks.

clue.text: Within five laps, Ericsson to pass

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A racing driver called Ericsson aims to overtake within five laps.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Ericsson is a Swedish racing driver, which suits the lap-counting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse; both verbs mean to go by.

clue.text: Regularly drained cocktails, white wines

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the following word, the even ones here

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, as in the Singapore Sling

explanation.surface: Someone has been steadily knocking back cocktails and white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape and the white wine made from it, chiefly in Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: I say! A member of the Parachute Regiment turned native

indicators.note: turned means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: oh is an exclamation like I say!
a para is a soldier in the Parachute Regiment

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as a paratrooper goes native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like part of the phrase 'turned native', but it reverses OH A PARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: In Australia, bend to pick up shilling following Rod's partner

definitions.text: In Australia, bend to pick up

indicators.note: the shilling comes after the partner in the answer

parts.note: Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer whose stooge was a puppet emu
bob is old British slang for a shilling

explanation.surface: An Australian stoops to pick up a coin, after Rod's partner has done so.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a 1970s-80s British TV entertainer famous for his aggressive puppet Emu. A shilling was an old British coin, nicknamed a bob.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang, an emu-bob is stooping to collect litter, as an emu pecks the ground.

clue.text: Don Bradman finally caught in annual Test before close of play

indicators.note: the test piece comes ahead of the last piece
the letter is held inside the test, as a ball is caught in the hands

parts.note: the MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test for British vehicles

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the cricketer's name
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Don Bradman, the great Australian batsman, is caught out in a Test match just before stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like part of Bradman's name but is the definition: Monty Don is a British TV gardener. The MOT is Britain's annual vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty Don is the BBC gardening presenter, so this first name goes with Don.

clue.text: 007 outside Bagdad zoo (D'oh!) on manoeuvres, playing silly buggers

indicators.note: the spy's name goes around the outside of the shuffled letters

parts.note: 007 is the code number of James Bond

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: James Bond is outside a Baghdad zoo, groaning like Homer Simpson, while out on military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like part of the phrase 'on manoeuvres' but belongs to the fodder; 'outside' wraps Bond's name around the anagram. The Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band were a 1960s British comedy rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: The band's madcap, anarchic stage act made them famous as a group of musicians clowning about.

clue.text: Cartoonist's invoice pretty steep

definitions.note: read as cartoonist is, the noun followed by the verb

parts.note: a bill is an invoice
a tidy sum is a fairly large one, so tidy means pretty steep of a price

explanation.surface: A cartoonist complains that his bill is rather expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Tidy was a British cartoonist, known for 'The Cloggies' in Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Tidy was a prolific British newspaper and magazine cartoonist.

clue.text: See 1
If hyphenated, a close result?

parts.note: the clue's own number, ten, written with a hyphen between its digits gives a one-goal football score

explanation.surface: A query about whether a dash would make the outcome a tight one.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the clue number: 10 hyphenated becomes 1-0, a narrow football scoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-goal win to nothing is the narrowest possible football victory, hence a close result.

clue.text: See 7
Wife abandons sly individual to give support to artist

indicators.note: the wife leaves, so her letter is removed from the sly person

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on a crafty man to back a painter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds a painter's canvas, a support for an artist.

clue.text: In a Big Apple chain coffee bar, leave tip no matter how much

parts.note: at and in both mean located at a place
the Big Apple is New York, NY

indicators.note: the tip of the coffee chain's name, its last letter, is left off

parts.note: Costa is a British coffee shop chain

explanation.surface: In a New York coffee bar belonging to a chain, someone leaves a tip regardless of the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave tip' looks like advice about gratuities but removes the final A from COSTA, a big UK coffee chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever the price, regardless of how much it takes.

clue.text: Film barking dog pen, London

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A film set in a noisy London dog pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' suits the dogs but signals the anagram; barking mad is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1981 movie starring Henry Fonda and Katharine Hepburn won several Oscars.

clue.text: WC Fields's antepenultimate Bible

indicators.note: antepenultimate means third from last, picking that letter of the surname

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: The comedian WC Fields's third-to-last Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'WC' looks like the initials of the comedian W.C. Fields but is the definition. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lav, short for lavatory, is a toilet, which WC (water closet) also names.

clue.text: 9 lines composed for the 7th 27?

definitions.note: the clue numbered 27 gives the comedy troupe; the ? marks the nickname as a stretch

indicators.note: composed means the letters are arranged, as music is

parts.note: the number nine spelt out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nine lines of verse composed for the seventh member of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Innes of the Bonzo Dog band wrote songs for the Monty Python team and was often called the seventh Python.
explanation.definitionFit: Innes worked so closely with the comedy team on screen and stage that he earned the seventh-member nickname.

clue.text: Could be happiest last words

definitions.note: plural, matching the plural answer: inscriptions on tombs

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the happiest moment might also be one's final utterance.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription on a gravestone, the final words said about someone.

clue.text: Dipping into finances to repay grandpa?

indicators.note: the answer is found partway into the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Should one dip into savings to pay back grandfather?
explanation.walkthrough: The ? flags that grandpa is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is one example of a forebear in your family line.

clue.text: Actors Sean and Ms Kristel taking in a northern state

parts.note: Sean Penn is an American actor

indicators.note: the actress's name takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: Sylvia Kristel was the Dutch actress who starred in Emmanuelle

explanation.surface: Two actors, Sean Penn and Sylvia Kristel, take in a state in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennsylvania is one of the fifty US states, in the north-east.

clue.text: A jaunty rhythm inspired by the Caribbean as an alternative to 29?

definitions.meaning: a cheerful, swinging cadence in speech or music

definitions.text: inspired by the Caribbean as an alternative to 29?
definitions.meaning: a fizzy soft drink sold in Britain with a tropical fruit flavour, a rival to the lemon-lime soda at 29

explanation.walkthrough: Lilt is a pineapple-and-grapefruit soft drink sold in the UK with a Caribbean theme; 29-across is a lemon-lime soda.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilt is a gentle rising rhythm, and Lilt is also a British brand of tropical fizzy drink.

clue.text: Re: Russia: I left, all upset — he provided cover

indicators.note: all these letters are upset, knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter I has left, so it is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about Russia: someone has quit and everyone is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' removes I from RUSSIA, leaving RUSSA; 'all upset' shuffles RE + RUSSA.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer, who sells policies to protect against loss, is someone giving financial cover.

clue.text: See 7
Young winger, on the fringes for City, getting rise of ten grand

indicators.note: the fringes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A young footballer playing on the wing for City gets a pay rise of ten thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a baby swan, a young bird with wings.

clue.text: Idle group, those without pity endlessly taking second hour off

parts.note: the as a determiner standing for those people

indicators.note: the second of the two matching letters is the one taken
off says that letter is removed
endlessly drops the final letter

parts.note: pitiless means ruthless

explanation.surface: A lazy gang of heartless people never stop, and take the second hour off.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RUTHLESS loses its last S, then its second H. 'Idle' looks like lazy but is Eric Idle of Monty Python, who created this Beatles-spoof band with Neil Innes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle co-created this mock-Beatles band, so it is literally the group belonging to Idle.

clue.text: Stole uniform before time in submarine

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a boa is a long scarf, a stole of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: A stolen uniform turns up just in time aboard a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German military submarine of the world wars.

clue.text: Merchant's partner's material stolen from 1D

definitions.meaning: James ..., who made films with producer Ismail Merchant
the substance poachers take from an elephant's tusks

explanation.surface: A trader's associate takes some stuff from an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant Ivory was a film partnership, and elephant tusks are made of this precious white material.

clue.text: Cleveland, arguably, was one; Lee Jackson came later

definitions.meaning: Carol Cleveland appeared so often with the Flying Circus team that she is sometimes counted as a member
the first word of the band name ... Lee Jackson, which goes before Lee Jackson

explanation.surface: Cleveland was perhaps one; Lee Jackson arrived afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol Cleveland was the regular actress in Monty Python's Flying Circus. Python Lee Jackson were a band whose 1970 hit 'In a Broken Dream' featured Rod Stewart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: a member of the comedy team, and the word heading the band's name.

clue.text: Robotic, plain-sounding Trump gave boring speech

definitions.note: past tense phrasal verb, matching the answer

parts.note: a drone is a robotic aircraft, a plane, here spelt as its sound-alike plain
Don is short for Donald, Donald Trump's first name

explanation.surface: Trump delivered a dull, robotic, monotonous address.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to speak in a monotone; going on and on that way makes a tedious speech.

clue.text: Priest abused drink

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman misused alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' looks like a verb but is a noun: a soda brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprite is a lemon-lime soft drink made by Coca-Cola.

clue.text: Senior Army bod, British, a contemptible person to Americans

parts.note: asshat is American slang for an idiot or jerk

explanation.surface: A senior British officer is regarded by Americans as an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is British slang for a high-ranking officer, from the gold braid on the cap.
